info.name: Digilux OTA Update System
info.description:
REST API collection for the Digilux Over-The-Air update system. Covers package management, deployment lifecycle, and device compatibility checks.

**Base URL:** `https://ds6nxf8ac5.execute-api.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/smarthome`

**Auth:** All requests require a Cognito ID Token from the `admin` group in the `Authorization` header.

**How to get a token:**
```
aws cognito-idp initiate-auth \
  --auth-flow USER_PASSWORD_AUTH \
  --client-id q7189jitfkk4ttesepkgls491 \
  --auth-parameters USERNAME=<email>,PASSWORD=<password> \
  --region ap-south-1 \
  --query 'AuthenticationResult.IdToken' \
  --output text
```
Paste the result into the `auth_token` collection variable.

variable.description: Cognito ID Token for an admin-group user
Populated automatically by the Create Deployment request
Populated automatically by the Get Upload URL request

item.name: Packages
item.description: Manage OTA software packages — upload artifacts, list available packages, and check status.

query.description: Filter by status: ACTIVE or PENDING
List all versions of a specific package (optional)

request.description:
Returns all packages. Filter by `status` (ACTIVE or PENDING) or `packageName` to list versions of a specific package.

Typically called after uploading a package to poll until `status` changes from PENDING to ACTIVE (usually < 5 seconds).

Step 1 of the upload flow. Returns a pre-signed S3 PUT URL valid for 1 hour.

After receiving the response:
1. PUT the binary to `uploadUrl` with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`
2. Poll `GET /packages?packageName=<name>` until `status` = `ACTIVE`

The `upload_url` collection variable is auto-populated by the test script.

**packageType options:** `CONTROLLER_FIRMWARE`, `CONTROLLER_APP`, `DRIVER`, `ZIGBEE_DEVICE`, `CONFIG`, `RULES`

**compatibleModels:** Empty array `[]` = compatible with all models.

response.name: 200 OK — Upload URL issued
response.body:
{
  "uploadUrl": "https://digilux-ota-artifacts.s3.amazonaws.com/application/controller-app/4.0.0/controller-app-4.0.0.tar.gz?X-Amz-Algorithm=...",
  "s3Key": "application/controller-app/4.0.0/controller-app-4.0.0.tar.gz",
  "expiresIn": 3600,
  "packageName": "controller-app",
  "version": "4.0.0",
  "packageType": "CONTROLLER_APP",
  "status": "PENDING",
  "instructions": "PUT your binary to uploadUrl with Content-Type: application/octet-stream. The package will be registered automatically within seconds of upload."
}

response.name: 409 Conflict — Version already ACTIVE

request.description:
Step 2 of the upload flow. PUT the binary artifact directly to S3 using the pre-signed URL from the previous step.

- **No Authorization header** — the pre-signed URL handles auth
- Set `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`
- Select your binary file in the Body > file tab
- S3 returns HTTP 200 with empty body on success

After this, run `List Packages` (with packageName filter) to confirm status moves to ACTIVE.

item.name: Device
item.description: Check what software versions are installed on a device and what updates are available.

request.description:
Returns the current installed versions and any available updates for the device.

- `deviceId` is the UUID from `digilux_device_inventory` (not the MAC-based IoT thing name)
- `availableUpdates` is empty if the device is on the latest compatible version
- `pendingJobId` is non-null if there is an active deployment in progress
- Version comparison uses semver integer tuples — `4.10.0 > 4.2.0`
- `compatibleModels: []` (empty) means the package applies to all models

**404** is returned if the OTA agent has never run on this device.

response.name: 404 Not Found — Device not in inventory

item.name: Deployments
item.description: Create and manage OTA deployments. A deployment pushes a specific package version to a device or device group.

request.description:
Creates an IoT Job to push a package version to a device or device group.

The `job_id` collection variable is auto-populated by the test script for use in subsequent requests.

**targetType options:**
- `THING` — single device, `targetId` = device UUID
- `THING_GROUP` — group name (e.g. `DGX-Canary`), `targetId` = group name

**rolloutStage options:**
- `CANARY` — max 2 devices/min, first 5 devices
- `BETA` — exponential from 2/min, ~10% of fleet
- `PRODUCTION` — exponential from 5/min, full fleet (default)

**Validation errors:**
- 400 if package is not ACTIVE
- 400 if device already has this version installed (THING only)
- 404 if package/version not found
- 404 if device not in OTA inventory

response.name: 400 Bad Request — Already installed
400 Bad Request — Package not ACTIVE

request.description: Returns all deployments ordered newest-first. Maximum `limit` is 100.

exec: pm.test('Job reached terminal state: ' + status, () => pm.expect(terminal).to.include(status));
console.log('Job still in progress — status:', status, '(re-run to poll)');

request.description:
Returns full status of a deployment including per-device progress.

**Job status values:**
- `QUEUED` — created, device not yet acknowledged
- `IN_PROGRESS` — device is downloading/installing
- `SUCCEEDED` — installed and health check passed
- `FAILED` — failed; see `deviceStatuses[id].statusDetail`
- `CANCELLED` — aborted by admin
- `REJECTED` — device rejected (precondition not met)

**NEEDS_RECOVERY** appears in `statusDetail` when installation failed AND rollback also failed. Requires manual/SSH device access.

response.name: 200 OK — NEEDS_RECOVERY (critical)

request.description:
Cancels the IoT Job for all devices not yet in a terminal state.

**Behaviour:** `force=false` (default) — devices already downloading or installing are not interrupted. Only QUEUED executions are cancelled.

Already-terminal devices (SUCCEEDED, FAILED) are unaffected.

item.name: Full Deployment Flow
item.description:
End-to-end sequence: upload package → wait for ACTIVE → check device → deploy → poll until done.

Run these requests in order. Variables are auto-populated by test scripts.

exec: console.log('Package not found yet — re-run in a few seconds');
console.log('Still in progress — re-run to poll again');

item.name: End User Updates
item.description:
User-initiated OTA update flow. The homeowner (Flutter app user) checks for available updates, gives consent, and tracks progress.

**Auth:** Regular Cognito ID token — no admin group required.
**Flow:** Check → Consent → Poll status

Users can only see and update their own devices.

request.description:
Returns all controller devices owned by the calling user and any available updates for each device.

- Ownership is determined by the `userId` in the Cognito JWT (`sub` claim)
- Only devices registered in `digilux_device_data` under this userId are returned
- A device with `otaStatus: NOT_REGISTERED` has never run the OTA agent
- Version comparison uses semver integer tuples — `4.10.0 > 4.2.0`
- `pendingJobId` non-null means an update is already in progress

response.name: 200 OK — Device not yet OTA-registered

request.description:
Records the user's consent and triggers the OTA update on their device.

**Security checks performed (server-side):**
1. Valid Cognito JWT with `sub` claim
2. `deviceId` UUID format validation
3. Device ownership — `deviceId` must be registered under this `userId` in `digilux_device_data`
4. Package must exist and be `ACTIVE` (admin must have uploaded it first)
5. Requested version must be strictly newer than the installed version
6. No update already in progress (`pendingJobId` must be null)
7. Rate limit — max 1 consent per device per 5 minutes

On success, an AWS IoT Job is created and the device will download the binary via HTTPS from S3.

`job_id` and `consent_id` are auto-saved by the test script.

response.name: 202 Accepted — Update queued
response.body:

  "consentId": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",

409 Conflict — Update already in progress
409 Conflict — Already installed
429 Too Many Requests — Rate limited

exec: console.log('Still in progress — re-run to poll again');

request.description:
Returns the current status of a user-initiated update.

**Security:** the `jobId` must belong to a consent record created by the calling user. Users cannot query other users' job statuses — returns 404 if not found or not owned.

**Status values:**
- `QUEUED` — device not yet acknowledged
- `IN_PROGRESS` — downloading/installing
- `SUCCEEDED` — installed successfully
- `FAILED` — failed; device may have rolled back
- `CANCELLED` — cancelled
- `REJECTED` — device rejected
